Recovery of corals in cool water
How rising sea temperatures starve corals

questions.context: Before the introduction of the uniform penny post in Britain in 1840, the cost of sending a letter depended on distance and the number of sheets, and was paid by the recipient. A pricing reform that transformed letter writing
The history of communication in Britain

Why young trees need frequent watering

The properties of crystals in jewellery
questions.answer: How a vibrating crystal revolutionised watchmaking
questions.why: Trọng tâm là tinh thể thạch anh thay đổi ngành đồng hồ. Khủng hoảng Thụy Sĩ chỉ là hậu quả.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Online videos are compressed before they are sent, because uncompressed footage would take far too much bandwidth. Compression software discards details the eye is unlikely to notice and stores only the changes between frames rather than every image in full. The trade-off is quality: if a file is compressed too heavily, fast action appears blocky and colours blur.
options: The compromise between file size and picture quality in video
questions.answer: The compromise between file size and picture quality in video
questions.why: Ý chính: nén video đổi chất lượng lấy dung lượng. Các lựa chọn khác lệch trọng tâm.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Smart home devices connect everyday objects, such as thermostats, lights and locks, to the internet so they can be controlled remotely. They bring convenience and sometimes lower energy bills, yet each connected object is a potential entry point for hackers. Security experts advise changing default passwords and updating firmware, although many manufacturers stop issuing updates after a few years.
options: Convenience and security risks of connected household gadgets
questions.answer: Convenience and security risks of connected household gadgets
questions.why: Đoạn cân nhắc tiện lợi và rủi ro an ninh. Mật khẩu và cập nhật chỉ là lời khuyên.
questions.quote: a potential entry point for hackers

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: The printing of banknotes involves a battle against counterfeiters. Modern notes contain several security features, including watermarks, colour-shifting ink, raised printing and threads woven into the paper. Each feature is chosen to be easy for ordinary people to check but hard for forgers to reproduce. Central banks redesign their notes every few years to stay one step ahead of criminals.
options: The materials used in making paper
Security features used to protect banknotes from forgery
questions.answer: Security features used to protect banknotes from forgery
questions.why: Ý chính là các đặc điểm an ninh của tiền giấy. Thiết kế lại chỉ là chi tiết nhỏ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: Tunnel boring machines can drill through rock and soil while building their own lining. At the front, a rotating cutting wheel grinds the ground, and the debris is carried back along a conveyor. Behind the cutters, robotic arms install curved concrete segments that form the tunnel wall. The machines can advance several tens of metres a day, far faster than traditional blasting.
options: How tunnel boring machines excavate and line a tunnel
questions.answer: How tunnel boring machines excavate and line a tunnel
questions.why: Trọng tâm là cách máy đào hầm khoan và lát vách. Tốc độ so với nổ mìn là chi tiết phụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Drones were developed for military use, but they are now employed in farming, filming and rescue. A farmer can fly one over a field to spot disease in crops that is invisible from the ground, while emergency teams use them to locate missing hikers by heat. Regulators restrict where they can fly, because collisions with aircraft and invasions of privacy are real concerns.
options: Everyday uses of drones and the rules that limit them
questions.answer: Everyday uses of drones and the rules that limit them
questions.why: Đoạn nói ứng dụng thường ngày của drone và các quy định. Mỗi ví dụ chỉ là một mảnh.
questions.quote: now employed in farming, filming and rescue

title: Headings Practice 5: Health and the Mind

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: Vaccines train the immune system without causing the disease. A weakened or inactive part of a germ is introduced, and the body produces antibodies and memory cells that respond rapidly if the real germ appears later. When enough people are immunised, the germ struggles to find new hosts, and even those who cannot be vaccinated gain some protection, an effect known as herd immunity.
options: The discovery of the first vaccine
Why some people cannot be vaccinated
How vaccination protects individuals and communities
questions.answer: How vaccination protects individuals and communities
questions.why: Đoạn giải thích cách vắc-xin bảo vệ cá nhân và cộng đồng. Phát hiện lịch sử không được nhắc.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin, the hormone that signals the body it is time to sleep. People who use phones late at night often take longer to fall asleep and feel less alert next morning. Some devices now offer a warm-toned night mode, though experiments suggest that the content of what we watch may disturb sleep as much as the colour of the screen.
options: The role of melatonin in the body
Screens at night and their uncertain effect on sleep
questions.answer: Screens at night and their uncertain effect on sleep
questions.why: Ý chính là màn hình đêm ảnh hưởng giấc ngủ nhưng nguyên nhân chưa chắc chắn. Melatonin chỉ là cơ chế phụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: A balanced diet matters, but the link between particular foods and health is hard to prove. People who eat more vegetables also tend to exercise more and smoke less, so it is difficult to separate causes. The strongest evidence comes from trials in which volunteers are randomly assigned to diets, though these are expensive, short and depend on participants following instructions honestly.
options: Why proving the effect of diet on health is difficult
questions.answer: Why proving the effect of diet on health is difficult
questions.why: Trọng tâm: khó chứng minh tác động của chế độ ăn. Thử nghiệm ngẫu nhiên chỉ là phương pháp được nhắc.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: Pain is not simply a signal sent from an injury to the brain. The brain decides how much pain to feel by weighing the signal against context, mood and expectation. Soldiers badly wounded in battle sometimes report little pain until they are safe, and people expecting a treatment to help often feel relief even when given an inactive pill.
options: The role of the brain in shaping the experience of pain
questions.answer: The role of the brain in shaping the experience of pain
questions.why: Ý chính là não điều chỉnh cảm giác đau. Binh sĩ và thuốc giả dược chỉ là ví dụ.
questions.quote: The brain decides how much pain to feel

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Handwashing is one of the cheapest ways to prevent illness. In the 1840s, the doctor Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women died far less often in a maternity ward whose staff washed their hands in a chlorine solution. His colleagues rejected the idea, and he was ridiculed. Only after germ theory was established decades later was his work recognised.
options: The treatment of women in hospitals
Maternity care in the nineteenth century
An early discovery about hygiene that was ignored
questions.answer: An early discovery about hygiene that was ignored
questions.why: Trọng tâm: phát hiện sớm về vệ sinh bị bác bỏ. Thuyết vi trùng chỉ nằm ở cuối đoạn.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: Mindfulness meditation asks people to observe thoughts and sensations without judging them. Trials suggest it can reduce symptoms of anxiety and prevent relapse in some people who have suffered repeated depression. Results are weaker when mindfulness is compared with other active treatments, and some participants report unpleasant experiences, so experts advise treating it as one option rather than a cure-all.
options: A balanced view of the benefits of mindfulness
The origins of meditation in Asia
questions.answer: A balanced view of the benefits of mindfulness
questions.why: Đoạn đánh giá cân bằng lợi ích của chánh niệm. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: one option rather than a cure-all

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: The gut contains hundreds of species of bacteria that help digest food, produce vitamins and train the immune system. Antibiotics can disturb this community, and some researchers think its imbalance may play a role in allergies and obesity. The evidence so far comes largely from animal studies, and claims that special yoghurts can repair the gut are far ahead of the science.
options: The gut's bacteria: promising but unproven claims
questions.answer: The gut's bacteria: promising but unproven claims
questions.why: Ý chính: vi khuẩn đường ruột hứa hẹn nhưng bằng chứng còn thiếu. Sữa chua chỉ được nhắc để bác bỏ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Loneliness harms health. Studies in several countries have found that people with few social contacts are more likely to develop heart disease and to die earlier than those with strong relationships, even after accounting for age and wealth. Researchers think chronic loneliness keeps the body in a state of stress, raising blood pressure and weakening the immune response.
options: The physical damage caused by social isolation
The role of the immune system
questions.answer: The physical damage caused by social isolation
questions.why: Trọng tâm là cô đơn gây hại sức khoẻ thể chất. Huyết áp chỉ là cơ chế.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Left-handed people make up around ten per cent of the population in most societies. In the past, children were often forced to write with the right hand, and the word for left in many languages has negative meanings. Research has found no consistent differences in intelligence or health, though left-handers may have a slight advantage in some fast-ball sports such as fencing and tennis.
options: The meaning of words for left and right
Attitudes to left-handedness and what research shows
Forced changes of hand in schools
The percentage of people with a dominant hand
questions.answer: Attitudes to left-handedness and what research shows
questions.why: Đoạn nói thành kiến với người thuận tay trái và kết quả nghiên cứu. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là mảnh nhỏ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: A child learning a second language does not usually confuse the two. Bilingual children may mix words at first, but they soon learn to separate the systems and switch between them. Some studies suggest that managing two languages strengthens the brain's ability to focus and ignore distractions, although larger studies have been unable to confirm a strong effect.
options: How children learn their first words
The cognitive effects of growing up bilingual: promising but debated
questions.answer: The cognitive effects of growing up bilingual: promising but debated
questions.why: Ý chính: học hai ngôn ngữ ảnh hưởng nhận thức nhưng còn tranh cãi. Trộn từ chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: unable to confirm a strong effect

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: Many people believe that cracking the knuckles causes arthritis. In fact, the popping sound comes from gas bubbles forming in the fluid of the joint, and studies comparing habitual knucklecrackers with others have found no increased risk of arthritis. One doctor tested the idea on himself for sixty years, cracking only one hand, and found no difference between the two.
options: Debunking a common belief about joint cracking
questions.answer: Debunking a common belief about joint cracking
questions.why: Đoạn bác bỏ quan niệm sai về bẻ khớp. Thí nghiệm của bác sĩ chỉ là bằng chứng.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Sunlight allows the skin to make vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones. People in northern countries, those who cover their skin, and those who spend most of the day indoors are at greater risk of deficiency. Too much sun, however, raises the risk of skin cancer, so doctors recommend short exposure and, where needed, supplements.
options: Balancing the benefits and dangers of sunlight
questions.answer: Balancing the benefits and dangers of sunlight
questions.why: Ý chính: cân bằng lợi và hại của ánh nắng. Mỗi lựa chọn khác chỉ nói một vế.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Placebo effects are not merely imagination. When people are given inactive treatments, brain scans show changes in activity related to pain and mood, and the effect is stronger with larger pills, injections and treatments that are expensive. Some trials show benefits even when patients are told that the pill contains no medicine, which has surprised researchers.
options: The real physical effects of treatments with no active ingredient
questions.answer: The real physical effects of treatments with no active ingredient
questions.why: Trọng tâm: giả dược có tác động sinh lý thực. Chi tiết viên lớn và giá tiền chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Teenagers take more risks than adults, and part of the explanation lies in brain development. The regions responsible for emotion and reward mature earlier than those that control planning and restraint. As a result, adolescents are especially sensitive to rewards, particularly when peers are watching. Rather than blaming recklessness, some psychologists suggest channelling this energy into positive challenges.
options: Brain development and risk-taking in adolescence
questions.answer: Brain development and risk-taking in adolescence
questions.why: Ý chính: sự phát triển não giải thích hành vi mạo hiểm của tuổi teen. Áp lực bạn bè chỉ là yếu tố phụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Allergies appear to be more common in wealthy countries. One explanation, called the hygiene hypothesis, proposes that children who grow up in very clean surroundings encounter fewer microbes, leaving their immune systems prone to overreact to harmless substances such as pollen. Evidence is mixed, and researchers now prefer to speak of a lack of microbial diversity rather than cleanliness itself.
options: Wealth and health in different countries
A theory linking allergies to over-clean environments
How the immune system fights disease
questions.answer: A theory linking allergies to over-clean environments
questions.why: Đoạn nêu giả thuyết vệ sinh về dị ứng và những hạn chế. Phấn hoa chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Reading aloud to young children builds vocabulary long before they can read themselves. Parents who read daily expose children to words that rarely appear in everyday conversation, such as names of animals and unusual verbs. Children who are read to also tend to start school more eager to learn, although the effect partly reflects other advantages of homes where books are plentiful.
options: How reading aloud supports early language development
Starting school at an early age
questions.answer: How reading aloud supports early language development
questions.why: Trọng tâm: đọc to cho trẻ giúp phát triển từ vựng. Nhà có nhiều sách chỉ là lưu ý.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Noise is more than an annoyance. Long exposure to loud traffic or aircraft is associated with raised blood pressure and disturbed sleep, and children in schools near airports have been found to read less well. Quiet zones, double glazing and low-noise road surfaces can all help, but measures are costly, and complaints often come only after problems are severe.
options: The health effects of noise and ways to reduce them
questions.answer: The health effects of noise and ways to reduce them
questions.why: Ý chính: tiếng ồn ảnh hưởng sức khoẻ và cách giảm. Các lựa chọn khác quá hẹp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: Posture advice often exaggerates. People are told that slouching causes back pain, yet studies have not found a reliable link between how someone sits and their pain. Staying in any one position for hours, whether upright or not, seems more harmful. Experts therefore recommend moving regularly, standing up to stretch and walking during breaks.
options: Moving often matters more than sitting upright
questions.answer: Moving often matters more than sitting upright
questions.why: Trọng tâm: vận động thường xuyên quan trọng hơn ngồi thẳng. Nguyên nhân đau lưng quá rộng.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: Humour appears to help people cope with stress. Shared laughter bonds groups and releases tension, and patients who watch comedies report less pain in some studies. Yet researchers warn that humour can be harmful when used to hide feelings or to mock others. Therapists therefore distinguish between warm humour that connects people and sarcastic humour that keeps them apart.
options: The helpful and harmful sides of humour
questions.answer: The helpful and harmful sides of humour
questions.why: Ý chính: hài hước có mặt giúp ích và mặt gây hại. Từng lựa chọn kia chỉ là một mặt.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Caffeine is the world's most widely used stimulant. It blocks receptors for adenosine, a chemical that builds up during the day and makes us feel tired, so alertness increases for several hours. Moderate intake, around three or four cups of coffee, appears safe for most adults. Pregnant women and people with heart rhythm problems are generally advised to limit it, and drinking it late in the day can disturb sleep.
options: The popularity of coffee around the world
How caffeine works and who should take care
questions.answer: How caffeine works and who should take care
questions.why: Ý chính: cơ chế của caffeine và ai nên thận trọng. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

title: Headings Practice 6: Historical Episodes
topic: People, empires and turning points in the past

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: The Rosetta Stone, found in Egypt in 1799, carries the same decree written in three scripts: hieroglyphs, a cursive Egyptian script and Greek. Scholars could read the Greek, and by comparing the texts they began to decode the Egyptian. Jean-François Champollion made the decisive breakthrough in 1822, showing that hieroglyphs represent sounds as well as ideas, and opening ancient Egyptian writing to modern readers.
options: The discovery of Egypt by European travellers
The Greek language in the ancient world
The key that unlocked ancient Egyptian writing
questions.answer: The key that unlocked ancient Egyptian writing
questions.why: Đoạn nói về phiến đá Rosetta và việc giải mã chữ tượng hình. Cuộc đời Champollion là quá hẹp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: The Black Death reached Europe in the 1340s and killed perhaps a third of the population. Labour became scarce, and surviving workers demanded higher wages and better conditions. Landowners tried to hold wages down by law, but peasants often moved to find better offers. Many historians argue that the shortage of workers weakened the feudal system and hastened social change.
options: The origins of the plague in Asia
Medical treatments in the Middle Ages
Social consequences of a deadly epidemic
questions.answer: Social consequences of a deadly epidemic
questions.why: Ý chính là hậu quả xã hội của dịch hạch. Lương và luật phong kiến chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: The Inca built an empire of about ten million people without a written script or money. Instead they used knotted cords, called quipu, to record numbers, and a system of labour tax in which villages supplied workers to build roads, terraces and storehouses. A network of paved roads stretching over thirty thousand kilometres allowed runners to carry messages quickly across the Andes.
options: The size of the Andes mountains
Terraces and farming in South America
How the Inca ran a large empire without writing or money
questions.answer: How the Inca ran a large empire without writing or money
questions.why: Đoạn mô tả cách Inca quản lý đế chế khi không có chữ viết và tiền. Quipu chỉ là một công cụ.
questions.quote: without a written script or money

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: The Great Fire of London in 1666 destroyed about 13,000 houses and around eighty churches, yet only a handful of deaths were recorded. Rebuilding followed new rules requiring brick and stone rather than timber, and streets were widened to slow the spread of flames. Insurance, a rarity before, developed quickly as property owners sought protection against loss.
options: The number of people who died
Firefighting equipment of the seventeenth century
How a disaster reshaped the city and its building rules
questions.answer: How a disaster reshaped the city and its building rules
questions.why: Ý chính: đại hoả hoạn dẫn đến thay đổi quy tắc xây dựng và đô thị. Bảo hiểm chỉ là hệ quả phụ.
questions.quote: new rules requiring brick and stone

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Cleopatra is remembered as a seductress, but contemporaries emphasised her intelligence. She spoke several languages, including Egyptian, which none of her Macedonian-Greek predecessors had troubled to learn, and managed the finances of her kingdom skilfully. Her alliances with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony were political moves intended to preserve Egypt's independence against Rome.
options: The love affairs of Roman leaders
The political skill behind a famous queen's reputation
questions.answer: The political skill behind a famous queen's reputation
questions.why: Trọng tâm: tài năng chính trị của Cleopatra đối lập với hình ảnh quyến rũ. Ngôn ngữ chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: In 1912 the polar explorer Robert Scott and four companions reached the South Pole only to find that a Norwegian team under Roald Amundsen had arrived five weeks earlier. All five men died on the return journey, short of food and fuel. Historians contrast the two expeditions: Amundsen relied on dogs and skis learned from Arctic peoples, whereas Scott used ponies and man-hauling, which proved less effective.
options: The Arctic peoples and their skills
The use of ponies in the cold
Contrasting methods that decided the race to the South Pole
questions.answer: Contrasting methods that decided the race to the South Pole
questions.why: Ý chính: so sánh phương pháp dẫn đến kết quả cuộc đua. Cái chết của đoàn Scott là hệ quả.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: The Roman Empire's road network covered more than 80,000 kilometres, linking distant provinces to the capital. Built mainly for armies, the roads were constructed in layers of stone and gravel, with drainage ditches on either side. Messengers could cover about fifty kilometres a day, and merchants, pilgrims and ideas travelled along the same routes, binding the empire together.
options: Roman roads as a means of military and cultural unity
How roads were built in layers
The size of the Roman army
questions.answer: Roman roads as a means of military and cultural unity
questions.why: Trọng tâm là mạng lưới đường nối kết đế chế. Cách xây dựng chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late eighteenth century. Coal was plentiful, capital was available, and inventions such as the steam engine and the spinning machine raised output sharply. Cotton cloth production, once done by hand in cottages, moved into factories in rapidly growing towns. Wages rose slowly, but living conditions in many industrial cities were crowded and unhealthy for decades.
options: Why Britain industrialised first and what it cost
The invention of the steam engine
questions.answer: Why Britain industrialised first and what it cost
questions.why: Đoạn nêu nguyên nhân và cái giá của cách mạng công nghiệp. Mỗi lựa chọn khác chỉ là một chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: In 1215, English barons forced King John to accept Magna Carta, a charter that limited his power. Its most famous clauses promised that no free man could be imprisoned without lawful judgement and that the king could not raise certain taxes without consent. The document was soon annulled, but it was reissued repeatedly and later became a symbol of the idea that rulers are subject to law.
options: A medieval charter and its lasting symbolic importance
questions.answer: A medieval charter and its lasting symbolic importance
questions.why: Ý chính: Magna Carta và ý nghĩa biểu tượng lâu dài. Thuế khoá là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: The Polynesians settled islands scattered across the Pacific, from Hawaii to New Zealand, using canoes and no metal instruments. Navigators memorised star paths, read swell patterns and watched the flight of birds to find land. Their skill astonished early European sailors, who initially assumed the islands had been reached by accident. Modern voyages in replica canoes have shown that deliberate navigation was possible.
options: The navigation methods that allowed deliberate Pacific settlement
The tools of early European sailors
questions.answer: The navigation methods that allowed deliberate Pacific settlement
questions.why: Đoạn nói về kỹ thuật hàng hải để định cư có chủ ý. Xuồng mô phỏng chỉ là bằng chứng.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: Ancient Athens is often called the birthplace of democracy, but its system was limited. Adult male citizens voted directly on laws in an assembly, and many officials were chosen by lot rather than by election. Women, slaves and foreigners, who made up the majority of residents, were excluded. The Athenian example therefore shows both the appeal and the limits of early democracy.
options: The role of the assembly in Athens
The status of women in ancient Greece
The achievements and limits of Athenian democracy
questions.answer: The achievements and limits of Athenian democracy
questions.why: Trọng tâm: dân chủ Athens vừa có điểm tiến bộ vừa hạn chế. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: both the appeal and the limits

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan in the early thirteenth century, grew to become the largest connected land empire in history. Its armies relied on speed, with soldiers who rode several horses each, and on discipline. Once conquered, territories were often governed tolerantly: religions were respected, trade was protected, and a postal relay system carried messages across thousands of kilometres.
options: Military speed and tolerant rule behind Mongol expansion
The collapse of the Mongol Empire
questions.answer: Military speed and tolerant rule behind Mongol expansion
questions.why: Đoạn nói sức mạnh quân sự và cách cai trị khoan dung. Hệ thống bưu chính chỉ là một chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, cut about 13,000 kilometres from the sea journey between New York and San Francisco by avoiding the voyage around South America. Its construction cost the lives of thousands of workers, many from disease. A French attempt had failed in the 1880s, partly because the role of mosquitoes in spreading yellow fever and malaria was not yet understood.
options: The sea route around South America
French engineering in the nineteenth century
The human cost and challenges of building a waterway
New York as a trading port
questions.answer: The human cost and challenges of building a waterway
questions.why: Ý chính là khó khăn và thiệt hại khi xây kênh đào. Muỗi chỉ là một nguyên nhân.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Women gained the right to vote in New Zealand in 1893, the first self-governing country to grant it. The campaign was led by Kate Sheppard, who organised a petition signed by about a quarter of adult women in the country. Opponents argued that politics was unsuitable for women, but the Liberal government eventually passed the law, though women were not allowed to stand for parliament until 1919.
options: How New Zealand became the first country to let women vote
questions.answer: How New Zealand became the first country to let women vote
questions.why: Trọng tâm: New Zealand là nước đầu tiên cho phụ nữ bầu cử. Kiến nghị chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: The Berlin Wall divided the city of Berlin from 1961 to 1989. Built by East Germany to stop its citizens leaving for the West, it was guarded by watchtowers and patrols. Hundreds of people died trying to cross. In November 1989, after weeks of protest and a confusing announcement, crowds gathered at checkpoints and the guards allowed them through, and the wall was soon dismantled.
options: The rise and fall of a barrier that divided a city
questions.answer: The rise and fall of a barrier that divided a city
questions.why: Ý chính: bức tường Berlin được dựng rồi bị phá bỏ. Nỗ lực vượt tường chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: The Vikings are remembered as raiders, yet they were also traders and settlers. They sailed in shallow-hulled longships that could cross open sea and travel far up rivers, enabling both surprise attacks and long-distance commerce. They founded towns in Ireland, established farms in Iceland and Greenland, and reached North America around the year 1000, centuries before Columbus.
options: Vikings as explorers and traders as well as raiders
questions.answer: Vikings as explorers and traders as well as raiders
questions.why: Đoạn chỉ ra người Viking không chỉ là cướp biển. Thiết kế tàu chỉ là một chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Samuel Pepys, a government official in seventeenth-century London, kept a diary for nearly ten years. He recorded the Great Plague, the Great Fire and the court of Charles II, but also everyday matters such as dinners, quarrels with his wife and his fondness for the theatre. Because he wrote candidly, and in a form of shorthand, the diary remains a rich source for historians.
options: A private diary as a window on seventeenth-century life
questions.answer: A private diary as a window on seventeenth-century life
questions.why: Trọng tâm là cuốn nhật ký là nguồn tư liệu về đời sống thế kỷ 17. Từng sự kiện chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: The Great Wall of China is not one continuous wall but a series of walls, built by different dynasties over two thousand years. The best-known sections date from the Ming dynasty, which used stone and brick to guard against northern raiders. Contrary to popular belief, the wall cannot be seen from space with the naked eye, since it is long but narrow.
options: Myths and facts about the Great Wall
questions.answer: Myths and facts about the Great Wall
questions.why: Ý chính: đính chính những hiểu lầm về Vạn Lý Trường Thành. Triều Minh chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876, though others, including Elisha Gray, were working on similar devices and filed claims on the same day. Early lines carried only local calls, and few people could imagine the invention as more than a curiosity. Within a generation, however, exchanges linked cities, and the telephone had changed the way businesses operated.
options: The rivalry between Bell and Gray
The early history and rapid growth of the telephone
questions.answer: The early history and rapid growth of the telephone
questions.why: Trọng tâm: lịch sử ban đầu và sự lan nhanh của điện thoại. Tranh chấp bằng sáng chế chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. She coined the term radioactivity and discovered the elements polonium and radium. During the First World War she organised mobile X-ray units, known as little Curies, which helped surgeons locate bullets and shrapnel in wounded soldiers. Her long exposure to radiation probably contributed to her death in 1934.
options: The scientific achievements and wartime service of Marie Curie
questions.answer: The scientific achievements and wartime service of Marie Curie
questions.why: Trọng tâm: thành tựu khoa học và đóng góp thời chiến của Marie Curie. Mỗi lựa chọn khác chỉ là một chi tiết.
questions.quote: first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences

title: Headings Practice 7: Economics and Work
topic: Money, business and the world of work

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: Barter requires a double coincidence of wants: you must find someone who has what you need and also needs what you have. Money removes this obstacle by acting as a medium of exchange, a store of value and a unit of account. Societies have used shells, salt, metal discs and, more recently, electronic entries, provided that people trust that others will accept them in return.
options: Why money makes exchange easier than barter
The history of coins and metals
questions.answer: Why money makes exchange easier than barter
questions.why: Ý chính: tiền giải quyết hạn chế của hàng đổi hàng. Muối, vỏ sò chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: Supermarkets arrange their stores to encourage extra purchases. Essential items such as milk and bread are placed at the back so that shoppers walk past tempting displays; sweets sit near the checkout where tired children make requests; and the most expensive products are placed at eye level. Researchers estimate that such layout decisions can raise sales by several per cent.
options: The price of milk and bread
The rise of online grocery shopping
Store layouts designed to influence what shoppers buy
questions.answer: Store layouts designed to influence what shoppers buy
questions.why: Đoạn nói bố cục siêu thị nhằm tác động mua sắm. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: The gig economy offers flexibility: workers choose when to drive, deliver or complete small tasks through an app. But the arrangement often brings insecurity. Workers are usually classed as self-employed, so they may lack sick pay, holiday pay and a guaranteed minimum income. Courts in several countries have ruled that some platform workers should be treated as employees, and companies are appealing the decisions.
options: The flexibility and insecurity of app-based work
questions.answer: The flexibility and insecurity of app-based work
questions.why: Trọng tâm: tính linh hoạt đi kèm bất ổn của công việc qua ứng dụng. Phán quyết toà án chỉ là một phần.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: In 1637, tulip bulbs in the Netherlands reached prices equal to the cost of a fine house, then collapsed within weeks. Tulip mania is often cited as the first speculative bubble. Some modern historians argue that the story has been exaggerated, since few people were ruined and records are scanty, but it remains a popular warning about prices that rise because buyers expect others to pay more.
options: The cultivation of tulips in Holland
The cost of houses in the seventeenth century
A famous bubble and the doubts about the story
questions.answer: A famous bubble and the doubts about the story
questions.why: Ý chính: bong bóng hoa tulip nổi tiếng nhưng câu chuyện có thể bị phóng đại. Giá nhà chỉ là so sánh.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Comparative advantage explains why trade benefits both sides even when one country is better at producing everything. If a country is relatively more efficient at making wine than cloth, it gains by specialising in wine and importing cloth, leaving the other country to focus on cloth. Both end up with more of both goods than if each tried to make everything itself.
options: How specialisation allows all trading partners to gain
questions.answer: How specialisation allows all trading partners to gain
questions.why: Trọng tâm: lợi thế so sánh giúp mọi bên cùng có lợi. Rượu vang và vải chỉ là minh hoạ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: Interns are often unpaid, particularly in creative industries and politics, and critics argue that this favours young people whose families can support them. Those without such help may not be able to accept opportunities that could lead to a career. A few countries have introduced laws requiring pay for internships beyond a short period, though enforcement is uneven.
options: Unpaid internships and the fairness of access to careers
The cost of living for students
questions.answer: Unpaid internships and the fairness of access to careers
questions.why: Ý chính: thực tập không lương gây bất công về cơ hội. Luật trả lương chỉ là phản ứng.
questions.quote: favours young people whose families can support them

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: Economists measure unemployment as the share of people without work who are actively seeking it. The figure can mislead. People who have given up looking are not counted, and those working a few hours a week are classed as employed. Some governments therefore publish broader measures that include discouraged workers and part-timers who would like more hours.
options: Why headline unemployment figures can be misleading
questions.answer: Why headline unemployment figures can be misleading
questions.why: Trọng tâm: con số thất nghiệp có thể gây hiểu lầm. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ nắm một ý.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Franchises allow a business owner to sell the right to use a brand and system to local operators. The franchisee pays fees and follows set rules, gaining a recognised name and support, while the franchiser expands without investing in every outlet. Problems arise when the two sides disagree about fees, supplies or the right to open nearby competing branches.
options: How the franchise model works and where it causes conflict
questions.answer: How the franchise model works and where it causes conflict
questions.why: Đoạn giải thích mô hình nhượng quyền và xung đột. Từng lựa chọn khác quá hẹp.
questions.quote: gaining a recognised name and support

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Microchips are made in a few factories, mostly in East Asia, which creates a fragile supply chain. When demand surged and some plants closed temporarily in 2020 and 2021, car makers around the world had to cut production because a handful of cheap components were missing. Governments are now offering subsidies to build factories closer to home.
options: Dependence on a few producers and government responses
questions.answer: Dependence on a few producers and government responses
questions.why: Ý chính: chuỗi cung ứng mong manh vì phụ thuộc vào ít nhà máy. Ô tô chỉ là một ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: A four-day working week has been trialled in several countries. In many trials, employees were paid the same for fewer hours, and most firms reported unchanged or higher productivity, along with lower burnout and fewer resignations. However, participants tend to be small, office-based businesses that volunteered, so it is unclear whether the results would apply to hospitals, factories or shops.
options: Positive trial results for shorter weeks, with limits
questions.answer: Positive trial results for shorter weeks, with limits
questions.why: Đoạn nói kết quả thử nghiệm tích cực nhưng giới hạn khả năng áp dụng. Burnout chỉ là một kết quả.
questions.quote: unclear whether the results would apply

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: Advertising seeks not only to inform but to create associations. A drink is shown with laughing friends, a car with open roads, a bank with security. Psychologists say that repeated exposure builds familiarity, which people mistake for quality. Because consumers often cannot recall seeing individual advertisements, the influence is largely unconscious.
options: How advertising shapes preferences without conscious attention
questions.answer: How advertising shapes preferences without conscious attention
questions.why: Ý chính: quảng cáo tác động vô thức qua liên tưởng. Xe, ngân hàng chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Cash is declining in many countries as people switch to cards and phone payments. Sweden is the clearest example, where small shops and even churches accept electronic donations. Yet critics warn that a cashless society excludes people without bank accounts, creates risks if networks fail, and leaves users' spending habits visible to companies and governments.
options: Risks of moving away from cash
questions.answer: Risks of moving away from cash
questions.why: Trọng tâm: rủi ro của xã hội không tiền mặt. Thụy Điển chỉ là ví dụ minh hoạ xu hướng.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Cooperatives are businesses owned and run by their members, who may be farmers, workers or customers. Profits are shared according to participation rather than investment. The Mondragon group in Spain employs tens of thousands of people in a federation of cooperatives, and surveys suggest its workers enjoy greater job security than average, although decision-making can be slow.
options: Spanish industry in the twentieth century
Member-owned businesses and the example of Mondragon
questions.answer: Member-owned businesses and the example of Mondragon
questions.why: Ý chính: hợp tác xã do thành viên sở hữu, ví dụ Mondragon. Việc ra quyết định chậm chỉ là điểm yếu nhỏ.
questions.quote: owned and run by their members

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Inheritance shapes inequality. Wealthy families pass on money, property and social contacts, giving children a head start. Some economists propose higher taxes on large inheritances to level the playing field; others respond that people have a right to leave their money to whom they choose, and that heavy taxes encourage the rich to hide assets abroad.
options: The argument over taxing inherited wealth
How families pass on social contacts
questions.answer: The argument over taxing inherited wealth
questions.why: Trọng tâm: tranh luận về đánh thuế thừa kế. Giấu tài sản chỉ là luận điểm phản đối.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Seasonal tourism can strain small communities. In peak months, rents rise, roads clog and local services struggle, while in winter many businesses close and workers lose income. Some destinations now promote off-season visits through discounts and events, hoping to spread demand more evenly throughout the year. Local councils have also experimented with small tourist taxes to pay for services.
options: Uneven tourist demand and attempts to balance it
questions.answer: Uneven tourist demand and attempts to balance it
questions.why: Ý chính: du lịch theo mùa gây áp lực và nỗ lực cân bằng. Giá thuê nhà chỉ là một ảnh hưởng.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Women are underrepresented in senior business roles in most countries. Explanations include career breaks for childcare, differences in networks and bias in promotion decisions. Some companies have tried transparent pay scales and blind recruitment, in which names are hidden from application forms, and report modest gains, though researchers say lasting change requires altering workplace culture.
options: Attempts to address the shortage of women in senior jobs
questions.answer: Attempts to address the shortage of women in senior jobs
questions.why: Đoạn nói nguyên nhân và các nỗ lực khắc phục. Ẩn tên chỉ là một biện pháp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: Auctions are used to sell everything from artwork to radio spectrum. In an English auction, bidders raise their offers openly until one remains. In a sealed-bid auction, each submits one secret offer. Economists study these formats because they influence prices; a poorly designed auction can leave the seller with far less than the goods are worth, as some national spectrum sales have shown.
options: Different auction formats and why design matters
questions.answer: Different auction formats and why design matters
questions.why: Ý chính: các hình thức đấu giá và tầm quan trọng của thiết kế. Phổ tần chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: Minimum wage laws raise pay for the lowest earners, but economists have long debated their side effects. A simple model predicts that higher wages reduce the number of jobs. Yet several empirical studies in the 1990s found little loss of employment after modest increases, suggesting that employers may absorb costs through small price rises or lower turnover.
options: Evidence that minimum wage rises may not cost jobs
questions.answer: Evidence that minimum wage rises may not cost jobs
questions.why: Trọng tâm: bằng chứng cho thấy tăng lương tối thiểu có thể không mất việc. Mô hình đơn giản là quan điểm đối lập.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: Craft guilds in medieval towns controlled who could practise a trade. Members paid fees, followed standards and trained apprentices who worked for years before becoming masters. The system protected quality and prices, but it also limited competition and excluded outsiders. Many economists believe that its decline in the eighteenth century cleared the way for new industries and techniques.
options: The benefits and drawbacks of medieval trade guilds
questions.answer: The benefits and drawbacks of medieval trade guilds
questions.why: Đoạn cân nhắc cả ưu và nhược điểm của phường hội. Học nghề chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 20)
questions.context: Supply and demand explain why prices change. When more people want a product than there is available, sellers can raise prices; when stock exceeds demand, they cut them. Umbrella sellers know this well: a sudden shower will raise the price at a street stall within minutes. In practice, markets are shaped by other forces, such as taxes, regulation and the power of large firms, so prices do not always settle where simple models predict.
options: How supply and demand set prices, and where the model falls short
questions.answer: How supply and demand set prices, and where the model falls short
questions.why: Ý chính: cung cầu quyết định giá nhưng mô hình có giới hạn. Bán ô là ví dụ.
questions.quote: markets are shaped by other forces

title: Headings Practice 8: Language, Learning and Communication
topic: How people learn, speak and share information

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: Children usually acquire their first language without formal teaching. By the age of one they recognise the sounds of their parents' speech, and by two many are combining words. Remarkably, they make systematic errors, such as saying goed instead of went, which shows that they are discovering rules rather than simply repeating what they hear. Adults rarely correct these mistakes explicitly, yet children correct themselves in time.
options: The first words spoken by babies
Evidence that children discover grammatical rules for themselves
questions.answer: Evidence that children discover grammatical rules for themselves
questions.why: Ý chính: lỗi có hệ thống chứng tỏ trẻ tự khám phá quy tắc. Các lựa chọn khác quá rộng hoặc lệch.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 2)
questions.context: Spaced repetition improves learning by reviewing material at increasing intervals. Instead of studying a list of words for three hours the night before a test, a learner revisits it after a day, then after three days, then after a week. Each recall strengthens memory, and difficult items appear more often. Apps now schedule these reviews automatically.
options: A review schedule that makes memory last longer
questions.answer: A review schedule that makes memory last longer
questions.why: Trọng tâm: lặp lại ngắt quãng giúp nhớ lâu. Ứng dụng chỉ là công cụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: Idioms are difficult for learners because their meaning cannot be deduced from the words. To kick the bucket has nothing to do with buckets, and a person who spills the beans reveals a secret rather than clumsy cooking. Teachers advise learning idioms in context, through stories and conversation, because memorising lists seldom helps people use the expressions naturally.
options: Why idioms are hard to learn and how to approach them
questions.answer: Why idioms are hard to learn and how to approach them
questions.why: Đoạn giải thích vì sao thành ngữ khó và cách học. Câu chuyện chỉ là phương pháp được gợi ý.
questions.quote: cannot be deduced from the words

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: Pronunciation varies enormously within English. In some regions, the vowel in bath is long, in others short, and speakers of some dialects drop the letter h. These differences are not mistakes but patterns that reflect history and migration. Linguists point out that no accent is inherently better, although listeners often judge speakers by their way of speaking and may discriminate unfairly.
options: Regional accents as natural variation, with social consequences
questions.answer: Regional accents as natural variation, with social consequences
questions.why: Ý chính: giọng vùng miền là biến thể tự nhiên nhưng có hệ quả xã hội. Âm h chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: Reading speed matters less than comprehension. Many readers try to read faster by skimming, but studies show that comprehension falls quickly once speed rises beyond a modest level. A better habit is to preview the structure of a text, pose questions and pause to summarise. Speed then increases naturally as the reader becomes more familiar with the topic.
options: Understanding, not speed, as the key to better reading
questions.answer: Understanding, not speed, as the key to better reading
questions.why: Trọng tâm: hiểu quan trọng hơn tốc độ. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ nắm một ý nhỏ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: The invention of writing allowed knowledge to survive beyond a single lifetime. The earliest known script, cuneiform, began as clay tokens used to count grain and sheep in Mesopotamia, then developed into wedge-shaped marks pressed into tablets. Over centuries these signs came to represent sounds as well as objects, and eventually were used for laws, letters and poems.
options: The development of writing from simple accounting records
questions.answer: The development of writing from simple accounting records
questions.why: Ý chính: chữ viết phát triển từ ghi chép kế toán. Luật và thơ là các dùng về sau.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: Online translation has improved enormously, particularly for common language pairs. Systems trained on billions of sentences produce fluent results, yet errors persist: idioms are rendered literally, tone is lost, and ambiguous words are mistranslated when context is thin. Professional translators now often use machine output as a first draft, and spend their time correcting and polishing it.
options: Language pairs in the internet age
questions.answer: Machine translation: fluent but imperfect
questions.why: Đoạn đánh giá dịch máy: trôi chảy nhưng vẫn lỗi. Thành ngữ chỉ là một loại lỗi.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Body language accompanies speech, but its meaning varies between cultures. A nod means agreement in many countries, but in parts of Bulgaria and Greece it can mean the opposite. Eye contact signals honesty in some places and disrespect in others. Travellers who rely on gestures alone risk misunderstanding, so it is wise to observe local habits before assuming a meaning.
options: The importance of nodding in conversation
Cultural differences in the meaning of gestures
questions.answer: Cultural differences in the meaning of gestures
questions.why: Ý chính: cử chỉ mang nghĩa khác nhau giữa các nền văn hoá. Gật đầu chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Many students believe they have a single learning style, such as visual or auditory, and that teaching should match it. Yet reviews of the research have found little evidence that matching instruction to preferred style improves results. What does work is matching the method to the content: diagrams for geography, sound for music, practice for skills.
options: Doubts about the idea of fixed learning styles
questions.answer: Doubts about the idea of fixed learning styles
questions.why: Trọng tâm: không có bằng chứng ủng hộ phong cách học cố định. Ví dụ chỉ để minh hoạ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: Public examinations have been criticised for rewarding memory rather than understanding. Candidates sit in silence and write answers to unseen questions within a fixed time. Defenders argue that exams are fair because every candidate faces the same conditions and the marking can be checked. Alternatives, such as portfolios and projects, assess deeper skills, but they are costly to mark and open to unequal help at home.
options: The strengths and weaknesses of examinations as assessment
questions.answer: The strengths and weaknesses of examinations as assessment
questions.why: Đoạn cân nhắc ưu nhược của thi cử. Dự án và chấm điểm chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: Podcasts have grown quickly because they fit into moments when people cannot read, such as driving or washing dishes. Without visuals, the listener forms mental images, which some say creates a more intimate bond with the speaker. Production is cheap, so niche shows on very specific topics flourish; however, finding income is hard for all but the most popular.
options: Why podcasts have become popular and how hard they are to monetise
The cost of making a radio show
questions.answer: Why podcasts have become popular and how hard they are to monetise
questions.why: Ý chính: podcast phổ biến nhưng khó kiếm tiền. Hình ảnh trong đầu chỉ là một lý do.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Literacy rates have risen sharply over the past two centuries. In 1820, only about one in eight adults worldwide could read; today the figure is more than eight in ten. Progress has been fastest where governments expanded free primary schooling and where girls gained access to education. Still, hundreds of millions of adults remain unable to read, two thirds of them women.
options: The history of schooling in the 1820s
Global gains in literacy and the groups still left behind
questions.answer: Global gains in literacy and the groups still left behind
questions.why: Trọng tâm: tỉ lệ biết chữ tăng mạnh nhưng vẫn còn nhóm bị bỏ lại. Giáo dục nữ chỉ là một yếu tố.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Taking notes during a lecture helps learning only if done thoughtfully. Students who try to record everything often write without thinking. Those who listen, identify the main ideas and rewrite them in their own words retain more. Reviewing the notes within a day further strengthens memory, which is why many teachers encourage a short, structured summary after each class.
options: How to take notes that actually improve learning
questions.answer: How to take notes that actually improve learning
questions.why: Ý chính: cách ghi chép hiệu quả. Tóm tắt và ôn trong ngày chỉ là bước phụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Debating teaches more than winning arguments. Participants must research both sides of a question, anticipate objections and respond calmly to criticism. Teachers who have introduced debating clubs report gains in confidence and in the ability to separate evidence from opinion. Some even assign students to defend positions they personally reject, to encourage empathy.
questions.answer: Skills developed through school debating
questions.why: Trọng tâm: kỹ năng rèn qua tranh biện ở trường. Chỉ nhắc một kỹ năng là quá hẹp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Word order differs widely among languages. English places the subject before the verb and the object after; Japanese puts the verb at the end of the sentence; Welsh often begins with the verb. These patterns shape how speakers plan what they say. Learners accustomed to one order often make mistakes in another until the new pattern becomes automatic.
options: How differences in word order affect language learners
questions.answer: How differences in word order affect language learners
questions.why: Ý chính: thứ tự từ khác nhau gây khó cho người học. Mỗi ngôn ngữ chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Newspapers face declining readership as people turn to the internet for news. Online news sites and their popularity

The history of pictures in writing
questions.answer: Emoji as a replacement for tone and gesture, with risks

options: How dictionaries record changes in word use
questions.answer: How dictionaries record changes in word use

Teachers who turn historical events into stories report that pupils recall dates and names for longer. questions.answer: Why stories help learning, and the risk of inaccuracy

questions.quote: easier to remember than the same facts in a list

title: Headings Practice 9: Earth and Space
topic: Planets, geology, oceans and the universe

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: The Moon is moving away from the Earth at about 3.8 centimetres a year, roughly the speed at which fingernails grow. The same process is gradually slowing the Earth's spin, so days are becoming longer.
options: The speed at which fingernails grow
The length of the day in the past
How the tides are slowly pushing the Moon away
questions.answer: How the tides are slowly pushing the Moon away

questions.context: Earthquakes occur when stress built up along a fault is suddenly released. options: The movement of plates each year
The causes of earthquakes and how they are measured
questions.answer: The causes of earthquakes and how they are measured
questions.why: Đoạn nêu nguyên nhân động đất và cách đo. Mỗi lựa chọn khác chỉ là một phần.
questions.quote: stress built up along a fault

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 3)
questions.context: Mars once had liquid water. Dry channels, delta-shaped deposits and minerals that form only in water show that rivers and lakes existed billions of years ago. Today the planet's thin atmosphere cannot hold liquid water at the surface, though ice remains at the poles and underground. Missions are searching for signs that simple life may once have arisen in those ancient waters.
options: Evidence that Mars was once wet and the search for past life
questions.answer: Evidence that Mars was once wet and the search for past life
questions.why: Trọng tâm: bằng chứng sao Hỏa từng có nước và việc tìm sự sống. Khí quyển mỏng chỉ là lý do khô hạn.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 4)
questions.context: A total solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes exactly between the Sun and the Earth. By coincidence the Moon is about four hundred times smaller than the Sun but also about four hundred times closer, so the two discs appear almost the same size in the sky. For a few minutes, the Sun's faint outer atmosphere, the corona, becomes visible, a sight that has astonished observers for millennia.
options: The alignment that produces a total solar eclipse
The sizes of the Sun and Moon
questions.answer: The alignment that produces a total solar eclipse
questions.why: Ý chính: sự thẳng hàng tạo ra nhật thực toàn phần. Quầng sáng chỉ là hệ quả.
questions.quote: passes exactly between the Sun and the Earth

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 5)
questions.context: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest structure built by living creatures, stretching more than 2,000 kilometres along the coast of Australia. It consists of thousands of individual reefs, each made by tiny animals called coral polyps secreting limestone. The reef is home to hundreds of species of fish and sea turtles, and it can be seen from space.
options: Fish and turtles of the sea
The scale and structure of Australia's great reef
questions.answer: The scale and structure of Australia's great reef
questions.why: Đoạn mô tả quy mô và cấu trúc rạn san hô. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: largest structure built by living creatures

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: Comets are balls of ice and dust left over from the formation of the solar system. When one approaches the Sun, heat turns the ice to gas, which streams away as a glowing tail that always points away from the Sun, whichever direction the comet is travelling. Some comets return regularly, such as Halley's, which is visible from Earth about every seventy-six years.
options: What comets are made of and why they develop tails
The regular return of Halley's comet
The formation of the solar system
questions.answer: What comets are made of and why they develop tails
questions.why: Ý chính: thành phần sao chổi và cách đuôi hình thành. Sao chổi Halley chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 7)
questions.context: Rocks are constantly recycled. Igneous rocks form when molten material cools; weathering breaks them into sediment; the sediment is compressed into sedimentary rock; and heat and pressure may transform that rock into metamorphic rock. Eventually, any type can be pulled deep into the Earth and melted, beginning the cycle again. The whole process takes millions of years.
options: The continuous cycle through which rocks change type
questions.answer: The continuous cycle through which rocks change type
questions.why: Trọng tâm: vòng tuần hoàn biến đổi của đá. Các loại đá riêng lẻ chỉ là các bước.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. In the 1980s scientists discovered a hole over Antarctica caused by chemicals called CFCs, once widely used in refrigerators and spray cans. An international agreement, the Montreal Protocol, banned these chemicals in 1987, and the layer is slowly recovering, with full recovery expected by around the middle of this century.
options: An environmental problem that international action is solving
questions.answer: An environmental problem that international action is solving
questions.why: Ý chính: vấn đề tầng ozone đang được hành động quốc tế giải quyết. Lỗ thủng chỉ là một mốc.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: The oceans cover seventy per cent of the Earth's surface, yet the seabed remains less thoroughly mapped than the surface of Mars. Ships measure depth with sound waves, but covering such a vast area takes decades. A global project aims to complete a map of the entire floor, because accurate maps help in predicting tsunamis, laying cables and understanding currents.
options: The incomplete mapping of the ocean floor and why it matters
The seventy per cent of the Earth
questions.answer: The incomplete mapping of the ocean floor and why it matters
questions.why: Trọng tâm: đáy đại dương chưa được vẽ bản đồ đầy đủ và lý do cần thiết. Sóng âm chỉ là phương pháp.
questions.quote: less thoroughly mapped than the surface of Mars

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: Black holes are regions where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. They form when massive stars collapse at the end of their lives. Although they cannot be seen directly, astronomers detect them through their effect on nearby stars and gas, which heat up and glow as they spiral inwards. In 2019 scientists published the first image of a black hole's shadow.
options: How black holes form and how they are detected
The first photograph of a black hole
questions.answer: How black holes form and how they are detected
questions.why: Ý chính: hình thành và cách phát hiện hố đen. Bức ảnh năm 2019 chỉ là một chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: The seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis, not by its distance from the Sun. When the northern hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight and longer days, giving summer, while the southern hemisphere experiences winter. In fact, the Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, in the middle of the northern winter.
options: Why the seasons occur, contrary to a common belief
questions.answer: Why the seasons occur, contrary to a common belief
questions.why: Trọng tâm: mùa do trục nghiêng, không phải khoảng cách. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: not by its distance from the Sun

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 12)
questions.context: Deserts expand when vegetation disappears. In the Sahel region south of the Sahara, drought combined with overgrazing and the cutting of trees for fuel has stripped soil of its cover, allowing wind to carry it away. Efforts to halt the process include planting a belt of trees across the continent and teaching farmers methods that protect the soil.
options: Desertification and efforts to slow it
questions.answer: Desertification and efforts to slow it
questions.why: Đoạn nói sa mạc hoá và nỗ lực ngăn chặn. Từng yếu tố chỉ là nguyên nhân hoặc biện pháp.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 13)
questions.context: Tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on the oceans. Most coasts experience two high and two low tides each day. The difference between them varies: when the Sun and Moon line up at new and full moon, spring tides produce the largest ranges, while at quarter phases neap tides are smaller. In places such as the Bay of Fundy, the range can exceed fifteen metres.
options: The gravitational pull of the Sun
The causes and patterns of ocean tides
questions.answer: The causes and patterns of ocean tides
questions.why: Ý chính: nguyên nhân và quy luật thủy triều. Vịnh Fundy chỉ là ví dụ.
questions.quote: two high and two low tides each day

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: The first artificial satellite, Sputnik, was launched by the Soviet Union in 1957 and transmitted a simple beeping signal for three weeks. Its success shocked the United States and began the space race, leading to the creation of NASA the following year. Within twelve years, the competition had produced a landing on the Moon.
options: The first people on the Moon
A satellite launch that triggered a race to the Moon
questions.answer: A satellite launch that triggered a race to the Moon
questions.why: Trọng tâm: vệ tinh đầu tiên khởi đầu cuộc đua lên Mặt Trăng. Tín hiệu bíp chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: Planets orbiting other stars, called exoplanets, were first confirmed in the 1990s. Today more than five thousand are known. Astronomers find them by watching for tiny dips in a star's brightness when a planet crosses its face, or for the slight wobble caused by a planet's gravity. Some lie in the habitable zone, where liquid water could exist.
options: Methods of discovering planets beyond our solar system
The first exoplanet confirmed in the 1990s
questions.answer: Methods of discovering planets beyond our solar system
questions.why: Ý chính: các phương pháp phát hiện ngoại hành tinh. Vùng sinh sống được chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: tiny dips in a star's brightness

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 16)
questions.context: Limestone caves form over hundreds of thousands of years as slightly acidic rainwater seeps through cracks and dissolves rock. Where water drips from the ceiling, it deposits calcium carbonate, building icicle-like stalactites, while those growing upward from the floor are stalagmites. Some caves also preserve ancient bones and paintings, offering clues to early human life.
options: The formation of caves and their contents
questions.answer: The formation of caves and their contents
questions.why: Trọng tâm: hang động hình thành và những gì chúng lưu giữ. Nhũ đá chỉ là một phần.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 17)
questions.context: The Sun is an average star, but it contains ninety-nine per cent of the mass of the solar system. Its core fuses hydrogen into helium, releasing the energy that eventually reaches Earth as light and heat. It has been shining for about 4.6 billion years and will continue for roughly five billion more, before swelling into a red giant.
options: The age of the solar system
The Sun's composition, energy and lifespan
questions.answer: The Sun's composition, energy and lifespan
questions.why: Ý chính: tổng quan về Mặt Trời. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là một chi tiết.
questions.quote: ninety-nine per cent of the mass

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 18)
questions.context: Hurricanes draw their energy from warm ocean water. options: The decline of storms over land
Why warm seas make hurricanes stronger
questions.answer: Why warm seas make hurricanes stronger
questions.why: Trọng tâm: đại dương ấm khiến bão mạnh hơn. Bão yếu đi trên đất liền chỉ là chi tiết.
questions.quote: draw their energy from warm ocean water

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 19)
questions.context: Fossils form when remains are buried quickly and minerals gradually replace the original material. Paleontologists estimate that only a tiny fraction of the species that ever lived have been found, and new discoveries regularly change ideas about evolution.
options: Why fossils are rare and the record is incomplete
questions.answer: Why fossils are rare and the record is incomplete
questions.why: Ý chính: hoá thạch hiếm và hồ sơ không đầy đủ. Các lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

options: Rain and sunlight in the tropics
The colours from red to violet
The optical process that produces a rainbow
questions.answer: The optical process that produces a rainbow
questions.why: Ý chính: cơ chế quang học tạo cầu vồng. Vị trí người quan sát chỉ là điều kiện.

title: Headings Practice 10: Cities, Transport and the Arts

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 1)
questions.context: The London Underground, opened in 1863, was the world's first underground passenger railway. questions.answer: The origins and influence of the first underground railway

Planners argue that safety, rather than encouragement campaigns, is the decisive factor.
options: Safe cycling lanes as the key to getting more people on bikes
questions.answer: Safe cycling lanes as the key to getting more people on bikes
questions.why: Trọng tâm: làn xe đạp an toàn là yếu tố quyết định. Chiến dịch khuyến khích là yếu tố phụ.

questions.context: Pedestrian-only streets have spread across European city centres since the 1960s. Shops initially feared losing customers who arrived by car, but studies often find that footfall rises and sales are maintained or increased, as people linger. Residents benefit from cleaner air and quieter streets, although delivery access and disabled parking require careful planning.
options: The benefits and practical challenges of car-free streets
questions.answer: The benefits and practical challenges of car-free streets
questions.why: Ý chính: lợi ích và thách thức thực tế của phố đi bộ. Mỗi lựa chọn khác chỉ là chi tiết.

options: The origin, spread and financing of opera
questions.answer: The origin, spread and financing of opera

options: Abstract art in the twentieth century
How the arrival of the camera pushed painters in new directions
questions.answer: How the arrival of the camera pushed painters in new directions
questions.why: Ý chính: máy ảnh khiến hội hoạ đi theo hướng mới. Trường phái cụ thể chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 6)
questions.context: Skyscrapers concentrate people and activity, but critics point to drawbacks. Supporters respond that dense building allows more people to live near jobs, reducing sprawl and the need for cars. The debate often turns on how well the surrounding streets are designed.
options: Arguments for and against very tall buildings
questions.answer: Arguments for and against very tall buildings
questions.why: Đoạn nêu cả lợi và hại của nhà chọc trời. Gió và năng lượng chỉ là các mặt hại.

questions.context: Airports are designed to move people smoothly, but their layout also shapes behaviour. questions.answer: How airport layouts balance passenger flow and commercial income

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 8)
questions.context: Rail travel in Japan is famous for punctuality: the average delay on the high-speed Shinkansen is measured in seconds. options: The reasons behind the reliability of Japanese high-speed trains
questions.answer: The reasons behind the reliability of Japanese high-speed trains
questions.why: Trọng tâm: lý do tàu cao tốc Nhật đúng giờ và an toàn. Đào tạo nhân viên chỉ là một lý do.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 9)
questions.context: Graffiti and street art can revitalise a neglected area, but they can also lead to displacement. questions.answer: How an artistic revival can drive out the original community
questions.why: Ý chính: nghệ thuật có thể khiến cư dân cũ bị đẩy ra. Giá thuê chỉ là cơ chế.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 10)
questions.context: Ferries remain an important form of transport in places where bridges would be too costly. questions.answer: The continuing role of ferries and their move towards electric power
questions.why: Trọng tâm: phà vẫn quan trọng và đang chuyển sang điện. Venice và Istanbul chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 11)
questions.context: The cinema industry was transformed by sound. The upheaval brought to film by the arrival of sound
questions.answer: The upheaval brought to film by the arrival of sound
questions.why: Ý chính: âm thanh làm thay đổi cả ngành điện ảnh. Diễn viên mất việc chỉ là một tác động.

questions.context: Traffic congestion costs cities billions each year in lost time and wasted fuel. The number of cars on roads
questions.answer: Why road building fails and how charging drivers can help
questions.why: Trọng tâm: xây thêm đường không giải quyết, thu phí mới giúp. Doanh thu chỉ là chi tiết.

questions.answer: Museums balancing interaction and traditional scholarship
questions.why: Ý chính: bảo tàng tăng tương tác nhưng bị lo ngại về học thuật. Hòa nhạc chỉ là ví dụ.

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 14)
questions.context: Public parks were created in the nineteenth century as green spaces for city dwellers suffering from overcrowding and pollution. New York's Central Park, designed in 1858, offered meadows, woods and lakes within walking distance of millions. Research shows that people who live near parks report lower stress and take more exercise, and property values nearby tend to rise.
options: The origins and benefits of urban parks
questions.answer: The origins and benefits of urban parks

questions.prompt: Choose the best heading for this paragraph. (Paragraph 15)
questions.context: The guitar evolved from earlier stringed instruments in Spain and has since spread to nearly every musical culture. Acoustic guitars rely on a hollow body to amplify the strings, while electric guitars use magnetic pickups and amplifiers. The electric version, popular since the 1950s, shaped rock music, and players such as Jimi Hendrix pushed it into new sounds.
options: The development of the guitar from acoustic to electric
questions.answer: The development of the guitar from acoustic to electric
